formula: Approximate or general information + more precisely + exact information

formulas.formula: Approximate or general information + more precisely + exact information

example: General information + more specifically + narrower information More precisely Use More precisely to replace an approximate, general or slightly unclear statement with more exact information.
exampleZh: 使用 More specifically，把較廣泛的內容收窄，指出正在討論的具體部分、群體、種類、範疇或例子。使用 More precisely，把大概、籠統或不夠清楚的說法改得更準確。

examples.en: General information + more specifically + narrower information More precisely Use More precisely to replace an approximate, general or slightly unclear statement with more exact information.
examples.zh: 使用 More specifically，把較廣泛的內容收窄，指出正在討論的具體部分、群體、種類、範疇或例子。使用 More precisely，把大概、籠統或不夠清楚的說法改得更準確。
examples.highlight: General information + more specifically + narrower information More precisely Use More precisely to replace an approximate, general or slightly unclear statement with more exact information.

rules.zh: 核心表達本身只是 more specifically 和 more precisely。後面補充的子句、詞組、數字、時間或地點並不是固定表達的一部分。報告討論污染問題，更具體地說，是空氣污染。 會議很晚才結束——更準確地說，是晚上八時四十七分。 兩個表達本身已經完整。後面的內容只是補充所需資料。
rules.en: The core expressions are simply “more specifically” and “more precisely” The information following the expression is not part of the fixed expression. The report discusses pollution, more specifically air pollution. The meeting ended late—more precisely, at 8:47 p.m. Both expressions are already complete. The information after them simply supplies the required detail.

rules.zh: 這兩個表達並非只可以放在一個固定位置，而是可以出現在不同的自然位置。這間店舖售賣食品。更具體地說，它專門售賣進口零食。 數字接近百分之十五。更準確地說，是百分之十四點八。 這個課程培養溝通能力；更具體地說，它培養口語能力。 問題在最後階段出現——更具體地說，是在測試期間。 車程約為兩小時——更準確地說，是一小時五十二分鐘。 這項政策適用於辦公室職員，更具體地說，是接待員。
rules.en: The expressions are not fixed in one position They can appear in several natural grammatical positions. At the beginning of a new sentence General statement. More specifically / More precisely, + complete clause. The shop sells food. More specifically, it specialises in imported snacks. The figure was close to 15%. More precisely, it was 14.8%. After a semicolon General statement The course develops communication skills more specifically, it develops speaking skills. After a dash General information—more specifically / more precisely, + detail. The problem occurred during the final stage—more specifically, during testing. The journey took about two hours—more precisely, one hour and fifty-two minutes. Before a narrower phrase Broad phrase, more specifically + narrower phrase The policy applies to office staff, more specifically receptionists.

rules.zh: 部分僱員——更具體地說，是新入職的接待員——需要接受培訓。 這個句型會修正前面的說法，或使其更加準確。包裹重約兩公斤——更準確地說，是二點一八公斤。
rules.en: As a parenthetical expression Broad group—more specifically, narrower group—+ verb Some employees—more specifically, the new receptionists—need training. With “or, more precisely,” This pattern corrects or sharpens the information immediately before it. The parcel weighs about two kilograms—or, more precisely, 2.18 kilograms.

rules.zh: 通常把一個廣泛類別收窄。這個課程涵蓋科學，更具體地說，是環境科學。 通常用來提供準確的數字、時間、日期、地點、量度或經修正的說法。課程下月開始——更準確地說，是九月十四日。 兩者有時可以互換使用，但本練習採用以下最清晰的分別：【more specifically = narrower detail】 更具體的資料更準確的資料
rules.en: “More specifically” and “more precisely” have different main purposes More specifically normally narrows a broad category. More specifically The programme covers science, more specifically environmental science. More precisely normally gives an exact number, time, date, place, measurement or corrected description. More precisely The programme begins next month—more precisely, on 14 September. The two expressions can sometimes overlap, but this exercise uses the clearest distinction: more specifically = narrower detail more precisely = more exact information

rules.zh: 如表達放在句首，後面要加逗號。如表達在一個完整子句後引出另一個完整子句，應使用句號、分號或破折號。不要只用逗號連接兩個完整子句。
rules.en: Use suitable punctuation When the expression begins a sentence, place a comma after it. More specifically, the problem affected younger users. When it introduces a complete clause after another complete clause, use a full stop, semicolon or dash. The course covers communication more specifically, it develops speaking skills. Do not join two complete clauses with commas only. The course covers communication, more specifically, it develops speaking skills.

rules.zh: 詞語【Especially】表示某事特別重要、常見或明顯。目標表達【More specifically】則指出較廣泛內容中的確切部分。我喜歡戶外活動，尤其是遠足。 這個課程教授戶外安全知識，更具體地說，是如何閱讀山徑標誌。
rules.en: “More specifically” is not exactly the same as “especially” Especially highlights something that is particularly important, common or noticeable. More specifically identifies the exact part of a broader idea. More specifically I enjoy outdoor activities, especially hiking. The programme teaches outdoor safety, more specifically how to read trail signs. 1. General statement. More specifically, + narrower clause. 2. General statement 3. Broad phrase, more specifically + narrower phrase. 4. Broad group—more specifically, narrower group—+ verb. 5. Approximate statement—more precisely, + exact information.

rules.zh: 如要把較概略的說法改得更準確，可使用「概略陳述—或更準確地說（or, more precisely,）+ 精確資料」這個結構。
rules.en: Approximate statement—or, more precisely, + exact information.

rules.zh: 後面補充的內容可以是完整子句、名詞詞組、介詞詞組、數字、百分比、時間、日期、地點或量度。
rules.en: General statement. More precisely, + corrected clause. The following detail may be a complete clause, noun phrase, prepositional phrase, number, percentage, time, date, place or measurement.

benefits.zh: 你可以先提出主要話題，然後再告訴讀者自己確實指哪一部分。報告討論交通。更具體地說，它研究巴士服務。
benefits.en: They help you move from a general idea to an exact detail You can first introduce the main topic and then tell the reader exactly which part you mean. The report discusses transport. More specifically, it examines bus services.

benefits.zh: 讀者先接收整體概念，然後才看到詳細資料，因此較複雜的內容會更容易理解。
benefits.en: They make explanations easier to follow The reader receives the general idea first and the detailed information afterwards. This makes complicated information easier to understand.

benefits.zh: 說話時，你可以先提出大概的數字、時間或描述，然後自然地補充準確資料，不需要重新說整句。車程約為三小時——更準確地說，是兩小時四十七分鐘。
benefits.en: “More precisely” helps you correct yourself naturally In speaking, you may begin with an approximate number, time or description and then provide the exact information without restarting the whole sentence. The journey took about three hours—or, more precisely, two hours and forty-seven minutes.

benefits.zh: 你不需要只使用「部分職員」、「一個問題」或「稍後」等籠統說法，而可以指出確實的人物、問題或時間。
benefits.en: They help you avoid vague statements Instead of leaving the reader with a broad expression such as “some staff”, “a problem” or “later”, you can identify the exact people, problem or time.

benefits.zh: 這兩個表達能讓你先提出重點，再補充支持資料，使報告、文章和簡報更有組織。
benefits.en: They organise reports, essays and presentations clearly These expressions help you begin with the main point and then develop it with supporting detail.

benefits.zh: 你不需要每次都把表達放在句首，而可以按句子需要使用句號、分號、破折號、逗號或插入語，增加句式變化。
benefits.en: They give you more sentence variety You do not need to place the expression at the beginning every time. You can use a full stop, semicolon, dash, comma or parenthetical expression according to the sentence.
